title: Telling a Modern MCP Server From a Legacy One

questions.question: Before sending any other request, how does a dual-era client learn whether a stdio MCP server is modern or legacy?
options: It assumes every server is modern until a later request happens to fail
It sends a server/discover probe first and reads the shape of the reply
It reads a version banner the server prints to stderr when it launches
It opens two connections and always compares how long each takes to answer
questions.explanation: A dual-era client probes with server/discover before anything else: a DiscoverResult, a recognized modern error, or a non-modern outcome each point to a different era.

questions.question: A dual-era client on stdio probes a server and receives a JSON-RPC error with code -32022. What should the client do next?
options: Fall back right away to the legacy handshake for that particular server instead
Treat the server as permanently unreachable and stop trying to contact it
Retry the same request using a version the error itself lists as supported
Wait a fixed number of seconds, then repeat the identical request again
questions.explanation: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError is a recognized modern error, so the server is modern: the client retries with a version from data.supported instead of falling back to legacy.

questions.question: Which outcome of a server/discover probe means the server is modern but speaks a different version than the client asked for?
options: An unrecognized error the client has never once seen, with no version data
A DiscoverResult that lists exactly the version the client had requested
No response at all within the client's own configured probe timeout
A recognized version error that also names the versions it does support
questions.explanation: A recognized modern error such as UnsupportedProtocolVersionError still identifies a modern server, just one that needs a different mutually supported version.

questions.question: On the Streamable HTTP transport, how should a dual-era client decide whether a server that just answered with 400 Bad Request is modern or legacy?
options: Read the response body; a recognized modern error still means modern
Treat every 400 response as proof the server only speaks the legacy revision
Retry the exact same unmodified request until the server somehow accepts it
Close the connection and ask whoever configured it to try another server
questions.explanation: Modern servers also answer 400 for version, capability, and header errors, so a dual-era client inspects the body for a recognized modern error before assuming legacy.

questions.question: A client's cached assumption that a particular server is modern turns out to be wrong on the next call. What does the spec say the client may do?
options: Nothing at all; a cached era decision can never be revisited later on
Re-probe the server, since a cached era may be rechecked later if it fails
Permanently block that whole server address for every other client that connects
Switch every other cached server's era over to legacy as a precaution
questions.explanation: Clients should cache the era decision for the life of the process or origin, and may re-probe if that cached assumption later fails.

questions.question: What does 2026-07-28 remove that a client written for the current revision should never send to a modern server?
options: A tools/call request that names a tool the server has never listed
A server/discover request sent before any other request on the connection
A request opening the connection with a version and capability handshake
A resources/read request naming a URI the server does not recognize
questions.explanation: The handshake and the session it used to open a connection are gone in 2026-07-28; every request now carries its own version and capabilities in _meta.
